findings.title: Async legacy writes use the request context and get cancelled when the handler returns
findings.body: Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection launch the legacy write in a goroutine that derives its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (line 51 `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)`; same pattern at lines 110, 135, 163). The apiserver cancels that context as soon as the handler returns, which is immediately after the goroutine is spawned. The legacy backup write is therefore usually aborted with `context canceled` before it runs, so mode 3's safety-net write to legacy silently does not happen and the legacy-store metrics record spurious failures/timeouts. Detach the goroutine's context from the request (e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` to keep values, or a fresh background context) so it survives handler completion.

findings.title: Storage failures are recorded into the legacy metric and legacy writes into the storage metric
findings.body: On the Storage error-return path, Create calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` (line 45) and Update does the same (line 129) instead of `recordStorageDuration`. Conversely the DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records its result via `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` (line 166). As a result storage errors/latency are attributed to the legacy store and legacy-write errors to unified storage, making the per-backend error and latency metrics/dashboards wrong. Use `recordStorageDuration` for the Storage call and `recordLegacyDuration` for the Legacy call on every path.

findings.title: Delete records the object name as the resource `kind` metric label
findings.body: In the Delete success path the storage duration is recorded with the object name passed as the `kind` argument: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` (line 106). The third parameter of `recordStorageDuration` is the resource kind, so every deleted object adds a new label value, exploding metric cardinality and mislabeling the series. It should pass `options.Kind`, as all the other calls do.

findings.title: Async legacy-write failures are never logged
findings.body: The legacy-write goroutines capture the legacy error but only feed it to a metric and never log it (e.g. Create lines 55-56 `_, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...)` then `d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)`; same in Delete, Update and DeleteCollection). The previous synchronous implementation logged these failures with `log.Error`. Now a failed legacy backup write is invisible in logs, so operators cannot diagnose why the legacy copy is missing. Log the error inside the goroutine (using a logger not tied to the soon-to-be-cancelled request context).

findings.title: mode 3 integration tests race the asynchronous legacy write
findings.body: The new mode 3 subtests reuse `doPlaylistTests`, which after writing through the k8s API immediately reads the legacy `/api/playlists` endpoint and asserts the same UIDs are present (line 529), and `getFromBothAPIs` does a legacy GET right after each k8s write. Mode 3 writes to legacy asynchronously, so these assertions race the background write and can fail intermittently (and will fail deterministically while the request-context cancellation bug exists). The test needs to wait/poll for the legacy copy to appear (e.g. `require.Eventually`) rather than asserting immediately.

findings.title: Unit tests never assert the legacy (async) write and don't wait for the goroutine
findings.body: TestMode3_Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection set up expectations on the legacy store but never verify the legacy write occurred (no `AssertCalled`/`AssertExpectations`) and never wait for the goroutine. Because the legacy write is fire-and-forget, the tests pass even if the legacy path never runs, so the defining behavior of mode 3 (dual write to legacy) is not actually tested. The goroutine can also still be invoking the shared `*mock.Mock` and metrics registry after the subtest returns, which can cause data races/flaky failures under `-race`. Wait for the goroutine (channel/WaitGroup) and assert the legacy call was made.

findings.title: Delete stores the wrong logger in the context
findings.body: Delete does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` (line 97) using the base logger instead of the per-request `log` that carries name/kind/method fields, unlike Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection. Downstream storage.Delete error logs therefore lose the request-scoped fields, making them harder to correlate. Use `log` here as the other methods do.
